title: Mixed Grothendieck construction and coherent binary-product conventions
statement: Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], the coherent category of categories and its object and arrow decoding from [lem-coef-cat-infinity-opposite-involution], the limiting cones and exact image-cone preservation of [lem-coef-infinity-limits-products-pullbacks], the right-pinch comparison of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], and the homotopy-fiber model of [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection]. For quasicategories $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ in an ambient universe containing $\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}$, let $F:\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal B\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}$ be a coherent functor. A model of its mixed Grothendieck construction consists of a total quasicategory $\mathcal E$ with projections to both bases, full simplicial inclusions of the fibers $F(a,b)$, and object coordinates $(a,b,u)$, bijectively identifying the vertices of $\mathcal E$. The projections are inner fibrations, with coherent cartesian transport in $\mathcal A$ and cocartesian transport in $\mathcal B$, given by the actual functors underlying the edges of $F$ and the corresponding natural families of lifts. For objects $(a,b,u),(a',b',v)$ and base arrows $(\alpha,\beta)$, its canonical comparison is a weak equivalence from $\operatorname{Map}_{F(a,b')}(F(a,\beta)u,F(\alpha,b')v)$, lifted to the ambient universe, to the homotopy fiber over $(\alpha,\beta)$ of the actual map on mapping spaces induced by both projections. This comparison has constant base path and is represented by composition first with the specified cocartesian lift of $\beta$, then with the specified cartesian lift of $\alpha$; the two composition triangles are simplicial families on the entire mapping space. For use with this construction, a chosen binary product is a limiting coherent cone on the two-object discrete diagram; finite products mean binary products and a terminal object. A functor preserves binary products when every limiting cone of this shape is carried to its actual limiting image cone, with both apex and entire coherent transformation fixed. Thus the hypothesis that $F(a,-)$ preserves binary products refers to the full coherent functor $F(a,-)$ into $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ and to its canonical product cone, equivalently its canonical comparison to the product infinity category.
